problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a set of archival boxes into identical shipping crates. The items to be crated are as follows:

* Document set Alpha: volume 37 cubic feet
* Document set Beta: volume 39 cubic feet
* Document set Gamma: volume 57 cubic feet
* Document set Delta: volume 61 cubic feet
* Document set Epsilon: volume 56 cubic feet
* Document set Zeta: volume 46 cubic feet
* Document set Eta: volume 68 cubic feet
* Document set Theta: volume 42 cubic feet
* Document set Iota: volume 65 cubic feet
* Document set Kappa: volume 32 cubic feet
* Document set Lambda: volume 65 cubic feet
* Document set Mu: volume 54 cubic feet
* Document set Nu: volume 39 cubic feet
* Document set Xi: volume 61 cubic feet
* Document set Omicron: volume 66 cubic feet
* Document set Pi: volume 38 cubic feet
* Document set Rho: volume 33 cubic feet
* Document set Sigma: volume 49 cubic feet
* Document set Tau: volume 54 cubic feet
* Document set Upsilon: volume 67 cubic feet
* Document set Phi: volume 60 cubic feet
* Document set Chi: volume 59 cubic feet
* Document set Psi: volume 68 cubic feet
* Document set Omega: volume 56 cubic feet
* Archive collection A: volume 51 cubic feet
* Archive collection B: volume 70 cubic feet
* Archive collection C: volume 64 cubic feet
* Archive collection D: volume 44 cubic feet
* Archive collection E: volume 34 cubic feet
* Archive collection F: volume 49 cubic feet
* Archive collection G: volume 64 cubic feet
* Archive collection H: volume 62 cubic feet
* Archive collection I: volume 45 cubic feet
* Archive collection J: volume 51 cubic feet

Each shipping crate has a maximum capacity of 100 cubic feet. The coordinator must place all archival boxes into crates, utilizing the smallest possible number of crates. Every box must be assigned to precisely one crate, and the aggregate volume within any given crate must not surpass its volumetric limit.
